claims.text: High configurational entropy stabilizes a multi-element solid-solution phase against intermetallic formation or phase segregation.
High configurational entropy is associated with extensive chemical disorder and severe lattice distortion in these nanoparticles.
Severe lattice distortion causes low atomic diffusivity in high-entropy alloys.
Lattice distortion increases local energy barriers for atomic rearrangement.
Reduced atomic diffusion suppresses high-temperature phase separation and elemental segregation.
Entropy- and distortion-induced diffusion barriers suppress elemental leaching.
One-pot colloidal or laser-based synthesis can produce near-equiatomic nanoparticles with homogeneous atomic mixing and high configurational disorder.
An intermediate-temperature post-synthesis anneal can induce slight local chemical ordering without causing overall phase segregation.
Local chemical ordering modulates lattice distortion and diffusion barriers.
A controlled degree of short-range order can further pin the nanoparticle structure relative to the maximally disordered state.
Annealed nanoparticles will undergo less grain growth than rapidly quenched nanoparticles during high-temperature operation.
Annealed nanoparticles will retain a more homogeneous elemental distribution than rapidly quenched nanoparticles during high-temperature operation.
Annealed nanoparticles will retain catalytic performance better than rapidly quenched nanoparticles.
Rapidly quenched nanoparticles may show more gradual phase separation or compositional drift than partially ordered, annealed nanoparticles.
Atomic mobility is elevated over the stated catalytic and thermoelectric service-temperature ranges but can be counteracted by intrinsic diffusion barriers.
The proposed mechanism applies from 773–1173 K in catalytic service and over an extended range reaching 1923 K in thermoelectric service.
Intrinsic immiscibility of a chosen elemental combination can overwhelm entropy-based stabilization.

Statistically indistinguishable degradation in annealed and quenched samples, or failure of annealing to improve stability, would falsify a stabilizing contribution from local ordering beyond configurational entropy.
